title: Track, find your leak, review: the five-minute money routine

say: Track, find your leak, review: the five-minute money routine.
This is the video for module two of Managing Money in Daily Life.
The best tracking system is the one you will still be using in three weeks. A rough notebook filled every night tells you almost everything.
Use a paper notebook, your phone notes app, or Google Sheets if you like totals.

panel.heading: A record you will still keep in 3 weeks
items: Notebook, notes app or Google Sheets
Five columns: date, item, category, amount, paid by
Seven categories, no more at the start
About five minutes a day

say: Whatever you choose, use the same five columns: date, what you bought, category, amount, and how you paid.

panel.heading: A record you will still keep in 3 weeks

say: Keep categories few. Start with seven: food and household, transport, phone and data, bills, children and school, family and giving, and personal and wants.
The routine takes about five minutes a day.

say: During the day, note any spending above 100 naira as it happens. Two words and an amount are enough, like bread 1,200.

Count the cash in your purse
Put each entry in a category
Plan tomorrow's payments and cash

say: In the evening, scroll through today's transactions in your bank and wallet apps, and add anything you forgot.

say: Count your cash. Starting cash minus cash spent should equal what is left. If not, write the difference as unknown, so the gap stays visible instead of hidden.

say: Put each entry in a category, then look at tomorrow: what must be paid, and how much cash will you carry?

say: Aisha starts Tuesday with 6,000 naira cash. During the day her note reads: keke 400, gala and drink 700, relaxer stock 3,500, kids' lunch 1,000.

card.title: Closing one day: the cash check

say: Her cash spends add up to 5,600 naira.

card.title: Closing one day: the cash check

say: So she should have 400 naira left. But her purse has only 200.

card.title: Closing one day: the cash check

say: She writes the 200 difference as unknown. Then her wallet app shows a 1,500 naira data purchase she had forgotten.
Her real total is 7,300 naira. Without the evening check she would have recorded only 5,600, and missed about a quarter of the day.

card.title: Closing one day: the cash check

say: After two weeks, total each category and turn it into a percentage of all spending. Then look for leaks.
A leak is money that goes out in small amounts you did not really choose. Large costs are usually planned. Leaks hide in things that are small each time, but frequent.

panel.heading: Where leaks hide
items: Small daily data and airtime top-ups
Extra rides from leaving late
Snacks and drinks out of habit
Repeated POS and transfer charges
Small loans never recorded

say: Look at daily data and airtime top-ups, extra rides because you left late, and snacks bought out of habit.

say: Blessing found 19 small items under 800 naira in her personal and wants category. Together they came to 7,600 naira over two weeks.

card.title: Estimating a saving honestly
card.note: A realistic month, not the perfect 7,200.

say: That is 3,800 a week. With a cap of 2,000, she saves 1,800 naira a week.

card.title: Estimating a saving honestly
card.note: A realistic month, not the perfect 7,200.

say: Four perfect weeks would save 7,200. But she plans for real life and assumes she keeps the rule three weeks out of four. That is about 5,400 naira a month. Honest estimates are easier to meet.

say: Once a week, on the same day, take about twenty minutes. Total each category, and write the planned amount beside the actual.

panel.heading: The weekly review: plan versus actual
items: Total the week by category
Compare with your plan
Explain differences over 1,000 naira
Set next week's plan

say: For every difference larger than about 1,000 naira, write one honest reason. Kemi, a nurse in Abeokuta, spent 3,000 more on giving because of a cousin's naming ceremony she knew about but did not plan for.

panel.heading: The weekly review: plan versus actual
items: Total the week by category
Compare with your plan
Explain differences over 1,000 naira
Set next week's plan

say: Then decide next week's plan. A cost that comes most months is not a surprise. Give it its own line. A habit needs a simple rule.
A difference is information, not failure.

panel.heading: The weekly review: plan versus actual

say: Cut wants and waste first: snacks bought while waiting, daily data bundles, and extra trips.

panel.heading: Cut leaks, not what keeps you well
left: Daily data instead of a plan

say: But food for your children, transport to work or market, and health care are not leaks, even when they are large. Do not cut what keeps you well.

panel.heading: Cut leaks, not what keeps you well
left: Daily data instead of a plan

say: To remember. Pick a tool you will keep using. Check alerts and count cash every evening. Leaks hide in small, frequent spending. Fix one leak at a time with a clear rule. And review your plan against what really happened, every week.
